data.body:
MEASUREMENT WIDENED — the asymmetry is worse than this ticket first recorded, found while answering "why
does the openai arm show blank est. cost?" during the S10 live run.

I originally recorded this as "Anthropic rows silently unpriced while Bedrock prices fine". That is true
but UNDERSTATES it. Measured against the installed genai-prices with the same call shape `_price_row` uses:

    provider_id="anthropic", model_ref="anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6"           -> LookupError  (blank)
    provider_id="anthropic", model_ref="claude-sonnet-4-6"                     -> OK  $0.004500
    provider_id="openai",    model_ref="openai:gpt-5.4"                        -> LookupError  (blank)
    provider_id="openai",    model_ref="gpt-5.4"                               -> OK  $0.004000
    provider_id="openai",    model_ref="openai:gpt-5.4-mini"                   -> LookupError  (blank)
    provider_id="openai",    model_ref="gpt-5.4-mini"                          -> OK  $0.001200
    provider_id="bedrock",   model_ref="bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6" -> OK  $0.004950
    control: provider_id="openai", model_ref="gpt-4o"                          -> OK  $0.003500

SO: **only the BEDROCK prefix form happens to resolve. Anthropic AND OpenAI both read blank.** The models
are all perfectly well known to genai-prices — the bare forms price fine. The id is simply malformed by the
`provider:` prefix that `_price_row` passes through as `model_ref`, and `LookupError` (genai-prices
unknown-model signal) is then caught at usage_log.py:429 and turned into "unpriced" with no warning.

WHY THIS IS MORE THAN COSMETIC, and worse for this epic specifically: the CI provider matrix
[rebar:f124-f14a-fd62-4973] exists to compare providers, and its cost table would show BEDROCK WITH
FIGURES AND THE OTHER TWO ARMS EMPTY. A reader would naturally conclude Bedrock is the expensive arm, when
in fact it is the only arm being measured at all. That is a wrong-direction bias in exactly the comparison
the epic was built to inform — and it is why f124s cost figures had to be computed BY HAND from logged
token counts rather than read off the tooling.

The observable symptom is the `est. cost excludes N unpriced calls` line in CI job summaries, on runs where
genai-prices demonstrably knows every model involved.

This does not change the approach: still a provider-aware id translation decided by REGISTRY MEMBERSHIP
rather than a `split(":")`, because the Bedrock remainder (`us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`) is not
genai-prices own AWS id shape either. It does raise the priority: the defect silently biases a
provider-cost comparison rather than merely omitting a number.

AC1 should be read as covering ALL THREE providers, not just Anthropic — a test that fixes only the
anthropic prefix would leave OpenAI blank and the bias intact.
